source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 megawatts of IT capacity across three buildings, the second-largest declared power budget among Virginia data centers that disclose one.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, and only 25 of them publish an IT capacity figure. Those 25 total 1,603 megawatts, so Sterling alone accounts for 7.2 percent of the state's declared capacity, concentrated in one campus of three buildings and 1.18 million square feet of technical space. The scarce resource in this data is disclosure, not construction.

IT capacity is the number that bounds how many accelerators a site can host, which makes it the most useful figure a data center can publish for AI purposes. At a typical training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, 116 megawatts converts to roughly 2,900 racks. That is arithmetic, not a statement about installed equipment. The operator's specifications do not say what tenants run there or how much of the capacity is in use.

The published specifications also omit total power draw, PUE, cooling technology, grid interconnection details, and any constraints on expansion, and list no certifications. The suitability score of 80 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, and records announced expansion as missing. Whether power supply or grid availability in Northern Virginia currently limits this campus cannot be determined from what is published.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
